where: Section 2 (edge vs cloud paragraph) and Quiz Q5
problem: The text says edge computing 'keeps the line running during a wide area network outage'. The line keeps running because control sits in the local PLC, not because of edge computing. A student may conclude that edge computing is needed for production to continue.
fix: Say: 'Edge gives low latency and keeps local monitoring and analytics running during a wide area network outage; the PLC keeps the line itself running.' Use the same wording in the Q5 answer.

problem: 'OPC-UA is an integration name for exchanging plant data' is vague and the name is usually written OPC UA. It is an open communication standard, not just a name.
fix: 'OPC UA (Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture) is an open standard for exchanging plant data between levels; see Unit 3 for protocol details.'

problem: The text says 'Four building blocks appear in most Industry 4.0 designs' and lists four, then treats edge computing, cloud computing and security as further blocks. The count does not match the content.
fix: Either fold edge, cloud and security into the list and drop the number, or say 'Four core blocks are ...' and present edge, cloud and security as supporting infrastructure.

problem: The premise says the plant 'still sends only daily OEE to ERP', but the answer says 'the data is not feeding MES or ERP decisions'. This reads as a contradiction and can confuse the student.
fix: Say: 'It sends a daily summary, so ERP sees the result after the fact; nothing in the plant changes because of the vibration data. That is reporting, not the closed cyber-physical loop Industry 4.0 means.'

problem: The answer only expands the acronym and names the factors; it does not define what OEE measures, which is what the question asks.
fix: Answer: 'OEE is the fraction of scheduled production time that becomes good parts: OEE = (Good count × Ideal cycle time) ÷ Planned production time = A × P × Q, where A is availability, P is performance and Q is quality.'
